title: The Vector of the Deep
premise: Wendell Fairweather smuggles memories through the orbital ring of Meridian Station, but her true obsession is the derelict beacon she alone maintains — until it receives a distress call in a language dead for two centuries, sent by the cryoship Halcyon, whose two sleeping populations were supposed to be a myth. The signal reveals that station authorities have known for decades and plan to wake only their own chosen colonists, erasing the other half of humanity from history. Wendell must choose between loyalty to the smuggler crew who became her family and the truth owed to ten thousand sleepers; in the end she broadcasts the full memory archive to every mind on the station at once, forcing an open vote on who wakes, and stays behind aboard the beacon as the Halcyon's doors finally open.
about_author: Lena Ashgrove is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write fiction about signals nobody answers. She lives aboard a converted ferry with her partner and a stubborn antenna array she refuses to decommission.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A routine smuggling run past orbital customs: Wendell carries illegal memories sewn into her own recollections, trading banter with inspector Doss while hiding grief-work recordings for paying clients. The chapter establishes her skill, her loneliness, and the small warmth of the crew. Emotional beat: competent isolation — she is trusted with everything except herself.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Off-shift, she visits the ancient beacon she maintains in secret, patching its failing core with scavenged parts. Flashbacks reveal she found its commissioning records scrubbed years ago. Her only companion there is a maintenance drone she's named. Emotional beat: tenderness toward something abandoned, mirroring how she wishes someone would tend to her.

chapters.title: Crew of the Long Haul
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Aboard the smuggler ship Vesper, we meet the found-family: captain Ilsa Rook, engineer Tam, and memory-archivist Sef, who teaches Wendell dead languages as a game. Ilsa hints at one last big job to buy them all out of smuggling forever. Emotional beat: belonging, fragile and unspoken, the thing Wendell fears losing most.

chapters.title: A Voice in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The beacon erupts with a distress signal — and Sef identifies the language as Pre-Collapse Standard, extinct two centuries. The message is fragmented but unmistakable: a cryoship, the Halcyon, waking early and failing. Wendell realizes the beacon was built to listen for exactly this. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as myth becomes coordinates.

chapters.title: What the Archives Buried
chapters.summary: POV Sef. Digging through black-market archives, Sef finds evidence the Halcyon carried two populations — corporate charter colonists and blacklisted refugees — and that station founder families still hold the wake-lists. Someone has been quietly buying up every copy of the ship's manifest for decades. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: Customs Has Questions
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Inspector Doss detains Wendell, not about contraband but about anomalous transmissions from her sector. He offers quiet warning: certain names above his pay grade are asking. She lies well, but leaves knowing she's marked. Emotional beat: the first crack between her instinct to trust authority and her instinct to survive.

chapters.title: The Job That Wasn't a Job
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ilsa takes a lucrative contract to salvage 'derelict equipment' at coordinates Wendell recognizes as the Halcyon's drift corridor. Realizing Ilsa may be unwittingly working for whoever wants the ship silenced, Wendell must decide whether to confess what she knows. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling against truth before either word is spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Confession at the Airlock
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell tells the crew everything: the beacon, the signal, the buried history. Tam rages at the risk; Sef argues the sleepers deserve rescue; Ilsa goes silent, then reveals she took the job because the crew is broke and hunted. Emotional beat: family fracturing under the weight of a secret that belongs to everyone now.

chapters.title: Approach Vector
chapters.summary: POV Tam. The Vesper slips past a patrol cordon toward the Halcyon, running dark. Tam narrates the tension of the approach and glimpses the ship: kilometers of hull, frost-scarred, still transmitting its dying plea. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into wonder — the largest thing any of them has ever seen, and it is asking for help.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Heartbeats
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Boarding the Halcyon, they find cryo-bays divided by a sealed bulkhead: Charter Wing and Exile Wing. Life support fails in days. Wendell interfaces with the ship's dying caretaker AI, which begs her to choose which wing wakes — it can power only one. Emotional beat: horror at discovering the choice is real, structural, and already loaded.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Mercy
chapters.summary: POV Sef. The crew debates. Waking the Charter Wing means resources, legitimacy, negotiation leverage; the Exile Wing holds more people and no allies. Sef uncovers the final cruelty: the wake-lists the station elite bought were designed to overwrite the Exile Wing's existence entirely. Emotional beat: moral vertigo — every option saves someone and betrays someone.

chapters.title: Doss at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Doss tracks them to the Halcyon, but arrives without backup and, cornered, admits he's suspected the cover-up for years and kept silent out of fear. He offers Wendell a choice: walk away and he falsifies his report, or push further and they both burn. Emotional beat: unexpected kinship — even the law's face is a hostage inside it.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Buried
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Flashback chapter: Ilsa once worked security for the founding families and helped suppress an earlier inquiry into the Halcyon. She took the salvage job hoping to destroy the last proof of her complicity. She confesses to Wendell alone. Emotional beat: shame meeting grace — the leader who protected them all by betraying strangers.

chapters.title: Signal Jammed
chapters.summary: POV Tam. A station strike team jumps the cordon; the Vesper is crippled and the Halcyon's transmitter destroyed. The elite want the ship to die quietly with everyone aboard. Tam buys escape with burns that nearly kill him. Emotional beat: fury — the enemy isn't ignorance anymore, it's deliberate erasure.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Trapped, Wendell studies the beacon's original design and finds its purpose: not just listening, but broadcasting — a mass memory-cast built to imprint truth directly into minds across the station. It needs a human carrier willing to hold the entire archive. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Loading the Dead Language
chapters.summary: POV Sef. Racing the failing cryo-systems, Sef compresses the Halcyon's full record — voices, manifests, the refugees' last messages home — into a single transmission, teaching Wendell enough Pre-Collapse Standard to anchor it. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in urgency; language as a way of keeping the dead company.

chapters.title: The Vote They Never Scheduled
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell returns to the station and triggers the beacon. Ten thousand memories flood every mind at once: the refugees' faces, the founders' signatures on the erasure orders, the sleeping children. Chaos, then silence, then the station begins arguing — loudly, publicly, for the first time in generations. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth as a physical force.

chapters.title: Trial by Daylight
chapters.summary: POV Doss. The station convulses. Founding families fall, Doss arrests his own superiors, and an emergency assembly convenes to answer the question the broadcast forced open: who wakes? Wendell testifies, refusing to make the choice herself. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, then law scrambling to catch up to it.

chapters.title: Both Wings Open
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The assembly votes to reroute station power and wake both wings, rationing the transition over months. The Vesper's crew leads the first boarding parties. Ilsa surrenders to public judgment rather than flee, and the assembly weighs her confession alongside her rescue work. Emotional beat: costly repair — no clean absolution, only accountability and continuation.

chapters.title: First Breath, Two Hundred Years Late
chapters.summary: POV Sef. The first Exile Wing sleepers wake to a crowd of strangers holding signs in their resurrected language. Sef interprets a grandmother's first words — a question about whether anyone remembered — and answers yes. Emotional beat: grief and joy fused; remembrance made flesh.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Offered a seat in the new government and a place in the crew, Wendell declines both. She returns to the beacon, now officially commissioned at last, and volunteers as its resident keeper — the listener for whatever else the dark is still trying to say. Emotional beat: choosing the post nobody wanted because somebody must love it.

chapters.title: Vector of the Deep
chapters.summary: POV Wendell, epilogue. Months later, the beacon hums with traffic from a reconnected humanity. Doss visits with coffee; the Halcyon glows populated in the viewport. A faint new signal arrives from deeper space — same dead tongue, different source. Wendell smiles and opens a channel. Emotional beat: quiet resolve; the story ends where listening begins.
